elements.text:
Our change program paired every department with a trained super-user before
the first classroom session. Training followed a teach-the-workflow model:
role-based curricula built from the client's own configured processes, not
vendor screenshots, delivered in the two weeks before each go-live wave.
Adoption was measured, not assumed — login rates, task completion inside
the new system, and help-desk ticket themes were reviewed weekly for six
weeks after go-live, and departments below threshold received targeted
refresher sessions. [CLIENT]'s claims supervisors
co-taught every session, which doubled voluntary attendance.

Hypercare for [CLIENT] ran four weeks per wave with a
dedicated command center: floor-walkers in high-volume departments, a
fifteen-minute triage SLA for payroll-impacting defects, and a daily
stand-down that reviewed every severity-one and severity-two ticket.
Transition to steady-state support required two consecutive weeks under
agreed ticket thresholds, plus a signed knowledge-transfer checklist with
the client's application-support team. The hypercare package was included
in the [FEE] program fee. Reference: [REFERENCE_NAME], VP of Finance
Transformation.
